tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local replay extending the prior C5-C7 supersession contract. The slice compares two interrupted partial-write orderings for one authorized transition S1 from predecessor K/P1/G1 to successor K2/P2/G2 under authority epoch E2: A, predecessor is durably marked superseded before any durable successor or transition record exists; B, a transition/successor record is durable before the predecessor link is written. It derives the minimum reconstruction fields and visibility rules needed to avoid duplicate or lost logical effects and falsifies a weak recovery rule that treats either one-sided durable marker as sufficient proof of completion. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

baseline.initial_state: predecessor committed and has no accepted successor

steps_before_crash: crash before any separate durable transition record or successor record
ordering_A_predecessor_marker_first.authoritative_reconstruction_after_crash: predecessor says superseded_by S1 but there is no durable object proving S1's successor identity, payload digest/generation, authority epoch, or commit state
ordering_A_predecessor_marker_first.reason: The marker suppresses safe predecessor re-execution but does not prove what successor was authorized or whether any successor effect was issued. Completing an arbitrary S1 guess can mutate the logical effect; rolling the marker back can duplicate an already-issued-but-unacknowledged successor. A strict predecessor-marker-first protocol is therefore not recoverable from repository state alone unless the marker itself atomically embeds the full transition envelope, in which case it is already transition evidence and no longer matches this strict ordering.
minimum_fields_if_marker_is_used_as_the_: exact successor K2/P2/G2 including payload digest

steps_before_crash: durably write S1 binding predecessor K/P1/G1, successor K2/P2/G2, payload digest, authority E2, state=prepared
optionally durably stage K2/P2/G2 as pending and non-authoritative under S1
ordering_B_transition_successor_first.authoritative_reconstruction_after_crash: predecessor remains the accepted committed predecessor; S1 and any staged successor are visible only as pending intent
recovery: if predecessor is still committed_no_successor and authority E2 is current, CAS predecessor to superseded_by=S1
then mark S1 committed and successor accepted; exact retries reconstruct this same transition
if predecessor already names another accepted transition, abort/reject S1 as conflict rather than overwrite
never expose the staged successor as the accepted logical result until S1 is committed and predecessor link matches
ordering_B_transition_successor_first.safety_condition: A prepared successor/transition may be durable before the predecessor link only if it is non-authoritative until the predecessor CAS and final transition commit agree.

derived_minimum_recoverable_write_order: 1. Durably create a unique prepared transition envelope S1 containing exact predecessor, exact successor/payload digest/generation, authority epoch/fence and the expected predecessor no-successor version.
2. A successor record may be staged, but it must be marked pending/non-authoritative and bound to S1.
3. CAS the predecessor from the exact expected committed_no_successor state to superseded_by=S1; a different accepted successor is a hard conflict.
4. Commit S1 and make the successor authoritative only when predecessor->S1 and S1->successor both match; readers/retries require this triad for duplicate-success reconstruction.

5. If the crash occurs before step 3, predecessor remains authoritative and S1 can be retried/aborted safely. If it occurs after step 3 but before step 4, S1 plus predecessor link deterministically identifies the only successor that may be finalized.

weak_recovery_rule.rule: After a crash, if either predecessor.superseded_by is durable or a successor/transition-shaped record exists, infer the logical transition completed and return that side as authoritative.
falsification: Under ordering A the durable predecessor marker does not identify a trustworthy successor or prove that successor execution happened, so inferring completion can lose or mutate the logical effect.

Under ordering B a staged successor can exist before the predecessor CAS; treating it as complete allows a competing successor or the still-authoritative predecessor to coexist with two accepted logical results.
Only a transition envelope plus matching predecessor link and committed visibility state distinguishes prepared intent from accepted successor state.

observations: A one-sided predecessor superseded marker creates an ambiguity that cannot be resolved safely if the successor identity, authority and transition state were never made durable.
A successor/transition can be staged first without becoming a duplicate effect only when it is explicitly pending and readers gate authority on a successful predecessor CAS plus transition commit.

The recoverable protocol therefore needs a durable prepared transition envelope before the system interprets either side as an accepted supersession, followed by an exact predecessor CAS and triad-consistent finalization.
inference: For the exact abstract crash-boundary fixture tested, durable write ordering matters independently of idempotency-key identity. The safest reconstructible pattern is intent-first: persist a complete prepared transition envelope, keep any staged successor non-authoritative, CAS the exact predecessor, then expose the successor only after predecessor->transition->successor consistency is durable. A predecessor-only superseded bit or successor-only record is insufficient evidence of completion. This is an abstract local contract and is not evidence that any concrete Chat-exposed provider implements the required atomicity or visibility semantics.
